title: Marcos wants multisector nutrition project sustained
summary: President Marcos wants a multisectoral nutrition project to continue even after the end of its implementation this year, citing the need to sustain health measures and ensure the delivery of key…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has urged government agencies and local government units to sustain nutrition and health services for mothers and children beyond the Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project (PMNP).

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos wants a multisectoral nutrition project to continue even after the end of its implementation this year, citing the need to sustain health measures and ensure the delivery of key services in the midst of a growing population.

Launched in March 2023, the Philippine Multisectoral Nutrition Project aims to bring together health, nutrition, water and sanitation and early childhood services from different sectors and bring resources closer to communities.

The World Bank-supported program, covering prenatal care and micronutrient supplementation for pregnant women, breastfeeding, complementary feeding, improved diets for children and sanitation access, is set to end on Dec. 31.
Speaking at a gathering in Pampanga marking the culmination of the project, Marcos said the government has to continue taking care of children despite leadership changes.

“That’s why Ms. (UNICEF Country Representative Kyungsun) Kim, what you said to us, that each program has an ending, I was just discussing with (Health Secretary) Doc Edwin (Mercado) that we have to find a way so that this program has no ending,” the President said.

“We keep making babies. So, we have to keep taking care of them. It doesn’t matter if we are still here, the LGU (local government unit) changes leadership, we still have to continue, those children still need help,” he added.

Marcos noted that malnutrition remains a serious concern for many families, particularly in vulnerable and underserved communities. In 2025, about one in four Filipino children under five years was stunted, he added.
“We know improving nutrition involves more than providing adequate food. Families need access to health care, clean water, sanitation, other essential services,” the Chief Executive said.
“And the challenge now is ensuring that these services are responsive and consistently delivered, especially in communities where they are needed the most.”

Marcos said the nutrition project has reached 6.17 million beneficiaries in 235 participating municipalities. He reported that 549,000 children under five have been tracked and eventually served while 134 participating municipalities have recorded significant reductions in stunting after two years.
